Hi all —

Following up from our pilot wrap convo: PilotCo has ~$12,500 of unused pilot credits from the July trial. We need to close this out for accounting and ops so their next invoice reflects the final disposition. Proposed approach:

- Issue a credit memo for $12,500 to be applied against the open AR balance for invoice #2026-07-31 (preferred by customer).
- Accounting classification question: should this be recorded as contra-revenue (credit memo -> Sales revenue reduction) or treated as a marketing expense reversal (COGS/expense)?

Asks:
- Laura — can you confirm whether we should net the credit against AR or issue a refund in our systems? If netting, please confirm GLA mapping and whether AP needs to route the JE.
- Rishi — your recommendation on proper ledger treatment, tax/VAT implications (PilotCo has EU presence), and whether this triggers any deferred revenue adjustments.
- Trevor — can you confirm PilotCo is OK with an invoice credit memo rather than a cash refund? They mentioned preference during the close call but I want it on record.

Attached: draft credit memo and the mutual action plan for final signoff. If we can get signoff by Friday I can issue the credit the following week and sync with AR.

Thanks —

GLA mapping: pending Rishi confirmation, my tentative mapping would be: 4120 (Revenue Contra) for the credit, offset to 1205 (Allowance for Credits). If we go the refund route we'd hit cash/AP which is more work.

Laura / Michael —

Quick accounting note on this one: based on our records the pilot allowance provided to PilotCo was recorded as a sales allowance (contra-revenue) at the time of grant (account 4120) rather than as a COGS or marketing expense. Therefore the cleanest path is:

1) Issue credit memo and apply it to the outstanding invoice (AR netting).
2) JE to record the credit memo: Debit 4120 (Sales Revenue) / Credit 1205 (Allowance for Credits) — this nets revenue; do NOT post to COGS.
3) If any portion of the pilot had been prepaid by the customer and recorded as deferred revenue, we need to reverse deferred revenue accordingly — run a deferred revenue rollforward to confirm.
4) Tax/VAT note: for EU legal entities, credit memos reduce taxable revenue in the period of issuance. Trevor — please confirm your local VAT registration so we can include the correct tax annotation on the memo.

Threshold: because this credit exceeds $10k we need CFO notification/approval on the journal entry. I can draft the CFO note once Laura confirms the final GL codes.

Attached is a short note describing the JE and the CFO escalation text.

Rishi Malhotra
Controller, Redwood Inference
